Craniotomy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E-Intially she noticed b\/l swelling of lower limbs , gradual onset and progressive . Pitting type and extending upto knees .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot associated with shortness of breath\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAssociated with decreased urine output\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot associated with orthopnea and PND\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o chest pain , palpitations\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn view of pedal edema , patient visited local hospital and was told ,She had a stone in one of her kidneys and both her kidneys failed .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe used NSAIDS for over 3 months I\/v\/o low backache.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe was advised maintenance hemodialysis,but patient denied and was discharged on medications .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELater, pedal edema subsided after using medications .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe continued taking medications , but noticed loss of appetite, fatigue and generalized weakness .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o pus in urine , burning micturition , frothy urine .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAs she had generalized fatigue ,loss of appetite and elevated urea and s. creatinine ,she visited our hospital and was initiated on hemodialysis by placing central venous catheter in right internal jugular vein .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had 4 sessions of hemodialysis .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe went to Hyderabad and got A-V fistula on his left hand .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC\/o Low back ache and body pains .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC\/O abdominal distension since 5 days , sudden onset and progressed gradually . Associated with increased sob on lying down and abdominal tightness.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema is mild extending upto ankle joint.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o yellowish discoloration of eyes . SHORT II"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online e-log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through a series of inputs from an available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This e-log book also reflects my patient-related online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConsent and de-identification: The patient and the attenders have been adequately informed about this documentation and privacy of the patient is being conserved entirely. No identifiers shall be revealed throughout this piece of work.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E20 year old female who is a student came to casuality with c\/o -\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E* Pain abdomen since 2 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E* Vomitings since 2 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E* Hypopigmentated lesions over face since 4 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 2 days back, then she developed pain abdomen in epigastric region, radiating to back, relieved on bending forward, associated with vomitings - non bilious, non projectile ( 4 episodes) subsided on taking medicine.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of similar complaints in the past, diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, 5 months ago and treated accordingly. No documents available\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/O RTA 3 years back ( fracture to left femur)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ewhere she was diagnosed to have Type 1 DM for which she was on insulin ( subcutaneous, Inj.Mixtard 12 U - X-\u0026nbsp; 10 U) for a year.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient observed non compliance to insulin and was shifted to OHA by local hospital.(? Unknown drug)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient used OHA for 2 months and stopped in between and started on insulin in her own.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDue to pain abdomen, patient dropped taking insulin for a day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet- Mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite - Normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and Bladder- Regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep - Decreased due to pain\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddictions - None\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneral examination:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient is conscious, coherent and cooperative, moderately built and nourished, and is well oriented to time, place and person.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBMI- 25.6 Kg\/m2\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIcterus: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECyanosis: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClubbing: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKoilonychia: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELymphadenopathy: SHORT l"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;This is an online e-log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through a series of inputs from an available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This e-log book also reflects my patient-related online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConsent and de-identification: The patient and the attenders have been adequately informed about this documentation and privacy of the patient is being conserved entirely. No identifiers shall be revealed throughout this piece of work.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChief complaints:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 75 y\/o male, labourer by occupation, presented with chief complaints of:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ swelling over the abdomen since 6 years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ pain over the swelling since 7 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of presenting illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 6 years ago, then\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ he noticed a swelling above his stomach (epigastric region), which was peanut-sized and gradually progressed to the present size. The swelling was firm in consistency, non-mobile, and shows no signs of transillumination or fluctuation. It is aggravated on consuming food and relieved by rest.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ he developed pain over the swelling which was insidious in onset, stabbing type in nature, non radiating, aggravated on work and relieved on rest.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o fever, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, cough, wheeze, abdominal pain, distension, constipation, or varicose veins.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPast history:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo similar complaints in the past\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, tuberculosis, asthma, hypertension, coronary artery disease, epilepsy, or thyroid disease.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThree years back, the patient had left sided renal calculi and received shockwave lithotripsy as treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/o knee pain, on and off for 6 months, for which he used an unknown NSAID.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPersonal history:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet: mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite: decreased\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and bladder movements: regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep: adequate\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddictions:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ smoking since the age of 11(1 - 2 packs per day)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ chewing tobacco\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ toddy consumption (500 ml - 1000 ml per day)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E→ alcohol consumption (60 ml per day)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuit all addictions 5 years ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneral examination:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient is conscious, coherent and cooperative, moderately built and nourished, and is well oriented to time, place and person.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIcterus: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECyanosis: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClubbing: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKoilonychia: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema:
